The image shows a soybean stem/hypocotyl near the soil line. Key features:
- Reddish-brown to orange-tan discoloration on the stem
- A dark, circular lesion/spot visible on the stem
- Firm-looking tissue (not water-soaked)
- Damage at/near soil level

Top candidates: **Rhizoctonia** (reddish-brown dry cankers at soil line), **Phytophthora** (chocolate-brown stem discoloration from below soil), **Fusarium** (reddish-brown root discoloration).

Let me view reference images for these candidates.
The Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-left panel) looks extremely similar to the test image — same setting, reddish-brown stem lesion near soil held by fingers. Let me view a couple more to confirm.

None of those match. My initial prediction is **Rhizoctonia** — the reddish-brown stem lesion at soil level matches the reference nearly exactly.

Now reading the Attractor Guide:

Rhizoctonia is not listed as an over-predicted attractor, so no need to reconsider alternatives. My prediction stands.

**Reasoning summary:**
- Stem at/near soil level with reddish-brown to orange-tan discoloration and a distinct dark lesion spot
- Tissue appears firm and dry (not water-soaked, ruling out Pythium)
- Color is more reddish than chocolate-brown (ruling out Phytophthora)
- Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-left panel) is nearly identical to test image in appearance, context, and coloration
- Classic "reddish-brown, sunken, dry canker on hypocotyl at soil line" matching Rhizoctonia description
